claims.text: The target material is a multi-phase eutectic high-entropy alloy with a polished surface.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion at elevated temperature accelerates degradation relative to separate wear or corrosion exposure.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion promotes formation of micro-galvanic cells in the multi-phase alloy.
Simultaneous wear and corrosion mechanically disrupts the protective oxide layer.
Micro-galvanic cells contribute to accelerated coupled degradation.
Mechanical disruption of the protective oxide contributes to accelerated coupled degradation.
The nominal test specifies a wear rate of 10^-4 mm/s.
The nominal corrosive environment is a 3.5% NaCl solution.
Coupled exposure will increase total degradation.
Coupled exposure will increase wear rate by 20% relative to individual exposure.
Coupled exposure will increase corrosion rate by 30% relative to individual exposure.
The baseline consists of individual wear-only or corrosion-only exposure at elevated temperature.
The proposed boundary conditions are 400–600°C, a wear-rate range of 10^-5–10^-3 mm/s, and 1–5% NaCl solution.
A controlled comparison of coupled exposure against wear-only and corrosion-only exposures can test the hypothesis.
Failure of coupled exposure to produce significantly higher total degradation at p < 0.05 would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: Wear rate is presented both as an imposed test condition and as a measured response predicted to change by 20%. The controlled input should instead be a wear parameter such as sliding speed, load, distance, or contact pressure.
